chunks: And by this chain of narration, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from 'Asim ibn Hamid, from 'Umar ibn Hanzalah, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: O 'Umar, Allah grants the world to whom He loves and to whom He dislikes, but He does not grant this matter (authority/leadership) except to His chosen elite. You, by Allah, are upon my religion and the religion of my fathers Abraham and Ishmael; I do not mean 'Ali ibn al-Husayn nor al-Baqir (peace be upon them), even if these [others] were upon the religion of those [fathers].

key_terms.أَهْلَ صَفْوَتِهِ: His chosen elite / His purified ones

ai.seo_question: What is the distinction between worldly power and religious authority in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Fadail al-Shia underscores the Shia doctrine of *Ismah* (infallibility) and divine selection (*Ihtiyaj*), distinguishing between general worldly power granted to the righteous and unrighteous alike, and the exclusive religious authority (*al-Amr*) reserved for the Prophet's purified lineage. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that while 'Ali ibn al-Husayn and al-Baqir share the same core faith, the specific chain of leadership being discussed is distinct, highlighting the unique spiritual status of the Ahl al-Bayt as the inheritors of Abraham's pure monotheism.

en.badr-shahin: (The same previous series of relaters)… from al-Hasan bin Ali from Aassim bin Hamid from Omar bin Hanzhala

that Abu Abdullah (a) said: O Omar, Allah surely grants the pleasures of this world to everyone whether He likes or dislikes, but He does not grant this matter except for His choice. You, by Allah, are following my religion as well as the religion of my forefathers Abraham and Ishmael, not Ali bin al-Hussein or al-Baqir (a) although these are following the religion of those.
